candidates.text: Provides a central configuration management system using YAML files and Python namedtuples to guarantee type safety and immutability across pipeline stages.
- FR-1.1: The system shall read pipeline settings from `config.yaml` using a YAML reader utility in `src/utils/common.py`.

- FR-1.2: The `AppConfiguration` class (`configuration.py`) shall instantiate immutable `ConfigEntity` objects for each stage:
- `DataIngestionConfig`
- `DataValidationConfig`
- `DataTransformationConfig`
- `ModelTrainerConfig`
- `ModelRecommendationConfig`
- FR-1.3: The Logger module shall record pipeline progress, warnings, and errors to both stdout and standard log files.
- FR-1.4: The Exception Handler module shall catch runtime exceptions, capture traceback details, and format structured error reports.

candidates.text: - FR-2.1: The component shall download raw zip archives containing `BX-Books.csv`, `BX-Book-Ratings.csv`, and `BX-Users.csv` from a remote GitHub storage URL specified in configuration.
- FR-2.2: The system shall extract zip contents into `artifacts/dataset/raw_data/`.
- FR-2.3: Upon successful extraction, raw files shall be verified and moved to `artifacts/dataset/ingested_data/`.
Validates, cleans, and filters raw rating data to isolate statistically significant reader-book interactions.
- FR-3.1: The system shall load `BX-Books.csv` and `BX-Book-Ratings.csv`.
- FR-3.2: User Filtering Rule: The component shall compute rating counts per user and discard users with fewer than 200 total ratings ($\text{ratings\_count} < 200$).
- FR-3.3: Book Filtering Rule: The component shall compute rating counts per book title and discard books with fewer than 50 total ratings ($\text{ratings\_count} < 50$).
- FR-3.4: The component shall perform an inner join on filtered users and filtered books to create the final cleaned ratings dataset.

- FR-3.5: Output files shall be saved to:
- `artifacts/dataset/clean_data.csv`
- `artifacts/serialized_objects/final_rating.pkl`
Transforms cleaned tabular data into a 2D interaction matrix required for Collaborative Filtering algorithms.

candidates.text: - FR-4.1: The system shall construct a pivot table where rows represent unique Book Titles (`title`) and columns represent unique User IDs (`user_id`).
- FR-4.2: The system shall replace all $NaN$ entries with $0$ to populate missing user ratings.

- FR-4.3: The transformed pivot table and book title list shall be serialized to:
- `artifacts/serialized_objects/book_pivot.pkl`
- `artifacts/serialized_objects/book_names.pkl`
- `templates/book_names.pkl` (for Streamlit UI binding)

candidates.text: - FR-5.1: The component shall convert `book_pivot` into a Compressed Sparse Row matrix (`scipy.sparse.csr_matrix`).

- FR-5.2: The system shall initialize and fit a Scikit-Learn `NearestNeighbors` estimator with parameters:
- `algorithm = 'brute'`
- `metric = 'cosine'` (or Euclidean distance as defined in configuration)
- FR-5.3: The trained model instance shall be serialized and saved to `artifacts/trained_model/model.pkl`.
Provides inference functionality to search for nearest neighbor books and fetch corresponding cover art posters.
- FR-6.1: The engine shall deserialize `model.pkl`, `book_pivot.pkl`, and `final_rating.pkl`.
- FR-6.2: Given a input book title, the engine shall look up its row index in `book_pivot`.
- FR-6.3: The engine shall invoke `model.kneighbors(..., n_neighbors=6)` to retrieve the top 6 nearest neighbor indices (where the 1st neighbor is the query book itself).
- FR-6.4: For each of the top 5 recommended books, the engine shall query `final_rating.pkl` to extract the corresponding book image cover URL (`Image-URL-L` or `Image-URL-M`).
- FR-6.5: The engine shall return a dictionary/tuple list containing recommended titles and image URLs.
Provides an intuitive single-page web interface for end-users and administrators.
- FR-7.1: Book Selector Dropdown: Render a searchable dropdown populated with book titles from `templates/book_names.pkl`.

- FR-7.2: Recommendation Button: Render a "Show Recommendation" button. Upon clicking:
- Compute recommendations using the Recommendation Engine.
- Display recommendations in a responsive 5-Column Layout.
- Show the cover poster image above each recommended book title.
- FR-7.3: Train Button: Render a "Train" trigger button allowing developers/admins to re-execute the ML Training Pipeline on demand.
Built with Streamlit (`app.py`).

candidates.text: > [!NOTE] > This SRS document serves as the formal technical specification for the End-to-End Books Recommender System project. All future enhancements and modifications should align with the functional requirements and architectural design outlined herein.

skipped_sections.heading: 1.1 Purpose
items: This Software Requirements Specification (SRS) document provides a comprehensive overview of the requirements, architecture, data flow, functional features, and non-functional characteristics of the End-to-End Books Recommender System.

The system leverages Machine Learning (Collaborative Filtering using K-Nearest Neighbors) to deliver personalized book recommendations to users based on historical rating patterns, complete with automated pipeline execution, image/poster fetching, and cloud-ready containerized deployment.

skipped_sections.heading: 1.2 Scope
items: The Books Recommender System encompasses:
Automated ML Pipeline: Modular stages covering Data Ingestion, Data Validation & Cleaning, Data Transformation, and Model Training.
Recommendation Engine: Real-time inference engine based on $k$-Nearest Neighbors ($k=6$) to compute top-5 similarity scores and retrieve corresponding book cover posters.
Web Application: Streamlit-based interactive web frontend (`app.py`) allowing users to trigger model training, search/select books, and view recommendation results in a 5-column visual layout.
Containerization & Deployment: Dockerized runtime setup built on `python:3.7-slim-buster`, exposing port `8501` for deployment to cloud environments (AWS / Azure).

skipped_sections.heading: 1.4 References
items: IEEE Std 830-1998: IEEE Recommended Practice for Software Requirements Specifications.
Book-Crossing Dataset: Public dataset comprising books, users, and ratings data (`BX-Books.csv`, `BX-Book-Ratings.csv`).

skipped_sections.heading: 2.1 Product Perspective & System Architecture
items: The system operates as a self-contained, modular ML application. Below is the high-level architecture overview illustrating the separation between configuration, ML training pipeline, storage/artifacts, recommendation engine, and presentation layer.

skipped_sections.heading: 2.2 Product Functions Summary
items: Config & Infrastructure: Reads configuration parameters (`config.yaml`), generates strongly typed namedtuple entities, logs execution status, and captures custom runtime exceptions.
Data Ingestion: Downloads data archives from GitHub storage, extracts CSV datasets, and saves raw/ingested data.
Data Validation & Filtering: Applies thresholds to ensure statistical significance:
Filters out inactive users ($ratings < 200$).
Filters out infrequently rated books ($ratings < 50$).
Saves clean merged dataset and serializes `final_rating.pkl`.
Data Transformation: Constructs a sparse matrix pivot table (`title` $\times$ `user_id`), handles missing values ($NaN \rightarrow 0$), and serializes `book_pivot.pkl` & `book_names.pkl`.
Model Training: Transforms pivot table into a `csr_matrix` format, trains a `NearestNeighbors` model (brute-force algorithm, cosine distance metric), and serializes `model.pkl`.
Recommendation & Poster Generation: Computes $k$-nearest neighbors for any selected book title, queries image URLs from the dataset, and formats top 5 recommendations.
Streamlit UI: Offers dropdown selection, button controls, and a multi-column visual showcase.

skipped_sections.heading: 2.3 User Classes and Characteristics
items: End-User / Reader: Non-technical user seeking book recommendations via the web UI dropdown.
Data Scientist / Developer: Technical user responsible for re-training pipelines, updating threshold parameters in `config.yaml`, and maintaining infrastructure code.
